Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 109, verses 1–6:

Makki. It has ninety-four letters, twenty-six words, and six verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Abu Umar al-Harashi informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Abu Jubayr, from al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'd, that Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im narrated to them that he heard Jubayr ibn Mut'im say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:

"Would you like, O Jubayr, when you set out on a journey, to be among the best of your companions in appearance and the most abundant in provisions?" He said: I said: "Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then recite these surahs: Say: O you disbelievers (Qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun); When the help of Allah comes (Idha ja'a nasr Allah); Say: He is Allah, the One (Qul huwa Allahu ahad); Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak (Qul a'udhu bi-rabb al-falaq); Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind (Qul a'udhu bi-rabb al-nas); and begin your recitation with: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful (Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim)." [281] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/224; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/133, where it reads "begin every surah" instead of "begin your recitation".]] He said: Jubayr said: I was wealthy with much property, and I would travel with whoever Allah willed that I travel with, and I would be the most shabby in appearance and the least in provisions. Then, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me these and I recited them, I have been among the best of them in appearance and the most abundant in provisions until I return from that journey. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 13/414.]]

Abu al-Abbas al-Sulayti informed us, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying:

Abd al-Razzaq and Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ash'ari, traced back (yarfa'uhu) to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said to a man: "Recite Say: O you disbelievers when you go to sleep, for it is a declaration of freedom from polytheism." [282] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/462.]]

Ahmad ibn Abi informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying:

al-Quṣayni narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Wardan narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Say: O you disbelievers is a quarter of the Qur'an." [283] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/148.]]

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Mu'addil narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to me, from Mukhalid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Jalil, from Zirr, from Ubayy, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites the surah Say: O you disbelievers has recited a quarter of the Qur'an, the rebellious devils will keep far from him, he will be freed from polytheism, and he will be protected from the greatest terror." [284] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/462.]]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said: "Order your children to recite it when they go to sleep, and nothing will harm them." [285]

Ibn Abbas said: There is no surah in the Qur'an more grievous to the anger of Iblis than this surah, because it is monotheism and a declaration of freedom from polytheism.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Say: O you disbelievers, to the end of the surah.

It was revealed concerning a group of the Quraysh, among them al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth al-Zuhri, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, and Umayya ibn Khalaf. They said: "O Muhammad, come, follow our religion and we will follow yours, and we will make you a partner in all our affairs: you worship our gods for a year, and we worship your God for a year. If what you have brought is better than what is in our hands, we will have shared in it and taken our portion of it; and if what is in our hands is better than what is in your hands, you will have shared in our affair and taken your portion of it." He said: "God forbid that I should associate anything with Him other than Him." [286] [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 307; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/463.]]

They said: "Then touch some of our gods, and we will affirm you and worship your God." He said: "Wait, until I see what comes from my Lord." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: Say: O you disbelievers, to the end of the surah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then went in the morning to the Sacred Mosque, where the chiefs of the Quraysh were gathered. He stood over their heads and recited it to them until he finished the surah. At that, they despaired of him, and they harmed him and harmed his companions.

As for the reason for the repetition of the statement: the meaning of the verse is, "I do not worship what you worship" (present), "nor are you worshippers of what I worship" (present), "nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped" (future), "nor are you worshippers of what I worship" (future). This is addressed to those whom Allah, glorified is He, knew in advance would not believe. Most scholars of meanings said:

The Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs and in the patterns of their discourse, and among their methods is repetition, intending emphasis and clarification, just as among their methods is brevity, intending lightness and conciseness. For the speaker's and orator's movement from one matter to another is better than his confining himself in the situation to one matter. God Most High said: "Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?" [[Surah al-Rahman.]] "Woe on that day to the deniers" [[Surah al-Mursalat: 15.]] in more than one place in a single surah. He, glorified is He, said: "No! They will come to know. Again, no! They will come to know" [[Surah al-Naba: 4-5.]]; He said, Most High: "And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?" [[Surah al-Infitar: 17.]]; He said: "For indeed, with hardship is ease. Indeed, with hardship is ease" [[Surah al-Sharh: 5-6.]]. All of this is intended for emphasis. The speaker says: "Shoot, shoot!" "Hurry, hurry!" And from it is the hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the minbar one day and said: "The Banu Makhzum have asked permission to marry their daughter to Ali, but I do not permit it, then I do not permit it, then I do not permit it, for Fatimah is a part of me; what pleases her pleases me, and what troubles her troubles me." [287]

And from it is the saying of the poet:

"Why did you not ask the hosts of Kinda, on the day they turned their backs, 'Where, where is ours?'"

And another said:

"O Alqamah, O Alqamah, O Alqamah, the best of all Tamim and its most noble."

And another said:

"Near the peg of the ostrich to me, the war of Wa'il gave birth to Hayyan."

Then he said, in several verses of this qasidah:

"The war of Wa'il gave birth to Hayyan."

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib recited to me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muzaffar al-Anbari recited to me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari recited to us, for one of the Bedouin women:

"The men of her husband say, perhaps she will be consoled and content after him with another husband."

So she concealed in her soul what was not behind it: hope, and that truth is the best that is said.

"After my cousin, the lord of the people, Malik, shall I be brought to a husband who is fierce and dull?"

His companions related to me that Malik stayed and called his companions to depart.

His companions related to me that Malik was a fasting man, like the sharp edge of a polished blade.

His companions related to me that Malik was generous with what was in the saddle, not stingy.

Al-Qutaybi said: There is another aspect to it as well, namely that the Quraysh said: "If you wish that we enter your religion for a year, then you enter ours for a year," and this surah was revealed. So the repetition of the statement is for the repetition of the time. He said: There is another aspect as well: that the Qur'an was revealed piece by piece and verse after verse, so it is as if they said, "Worship our gods for a year," and Allah, Most High, said: "I do not worship what you worship," then after that they said, "Touch some of our gods," and Allah, Most High, revealed: "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, which is polytheism, and for me is my religion, which is Islam."

This verse has been abrogated by the verse of the sword. The people of Medina, Isa ibn Umar, and what Hafs related from Asim, and Hisham from the people of Syria, read "wa-liya dini" with a fatha on the ya'; the others read it with a sukun, and Abu Hatim with a kasra.

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib recited to me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muzaffar al-Anbari recited to me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Anbari recited to us, for one of the Bedouin women:

"The men of her husband say, perhaps she will be consoled and content after him with another husband."

So she concealed in her soul what was not behind it: hope, and that truth is the best that is said.

"After my cousin, the lord of the people, Malik, shall I be brought to a husband who is fierce and dull?"

His companions related to me that Malik stayed and called his companions to depart.

His companions related to me that Malik was a fasting man, like the sharp edge of a polished blade.

His companions related to me that Malik was generous with what was in the saddle, not stingy.

Al-Qutaybi said: There is another aspect to it as well, namely that the Quraysh said: "If you wish that we enter your religion for a year, then you enter ours for a year," and this surah was revealed. So the repetition of the statement is for the repetition of the time. He said: There is another aspect as well: that the Qur'an was revealed piece by piece and verse after verse, so it is as if they said, "Worship our gods for a year," and Allah, Most High, said: "I do not worship what you worship," then after that they said, "Touch some of our gods," and Allah, Most High, revealed: "Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, which is polytheism, and for me is my religion, which is Islam."

This verse has been abrogated by the verse of the sword. The people of Medina, Isa ibn Umar, and what Hafs related from Asim, and Hisham from the people of Syria, read "wa-liya dini" with a fatha on the ya'; the others read it with a sukun, and Abu Hatim with a kasra.
